newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO trade accusations over policemen.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO trade accusations over policemen.

text.p: Israel-PLO peacemaking appeared on Saturday to be headed for another setback over Israeli allegations that a senior Palestinian security official sent three police officers to attack Jews in the West Bank.
Palestinians deny the charge and accuse Israel of trying to divert attention from what they say are the Jewish state's own peace deal violations.
Israel's army arrested three Palestinian police officers in the West Bank this week, announcing it had thwarted an attack on Jews at a settlement near Nablus.

A government official said on Saturday Israel had "electronic evidence" proving that a top PLO security official ordered the attack. The official named the Palestinian but refused to speak on the record.

"Israel will not tolerate a situation in which policemen of the Palestinian Authority will serve as an instrument to kill Israelis," said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications chief, David Bar-Illan.

Netanyahu this week described the incident as a flagrant violation of Israel-PLO peace accords and the United States sent a message to the Palestinians telling them to take the Israeli charges seriously.
A PLO official said on Saturday the police officers were chasing men suspected of trying to smuggle drugs into parts of the West Bank Israel handed over to Palestinian control.

"The three policemen were in pursuit of a car in which armed men were trying to smuggle drugs into the Palestinian Authority's areas," said Colonel Khaled Tantash, a senior police official on the Palestinian military liaison committee with Israel.

"The Palestinian police...asked the Israeli police to allow them to jointly interrogate the three detained Palestinian policemen, in line with the agreement, but the Israeli police refused," he told reporters at a news conference in Ramallah.

Netanyahu sent his Shin Bet security chief Ami Ayalon to Gaza on Thursday to press Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to take quick action. A Palestinian official said Ayalon gave Arafat the videotaped confession of one of the officers.

"We received the videotape of the so-called confession of this person. We are taking it very seriously. We are investigating very seriously and we demanded that the three soldiers (policemen) be handed over to us," Palestinian cabinet minister Nabil Shaath told Channel Two television.
But he stressed the informaton was "not solid", saying it was unclear under what conditions the confessions were made.
Arafat told reporters in self-ruled Ramallah after his weekly cabinet meeting on Friday night:
"It's part of a comprehensive campaign launched by the Israelis against the Palestinian Authority."
Palestinian police operate in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under Israel-PLO peace deals reached since 1993.

Security cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian troops outlined in the deals has broken down since March when the Jewish state started building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, plunging peacemaking into crisis.
The impasse has been punctuated by clashes between Israeli troops and Arab protesters in Hebron and other West Bank towns. Netanyahu has accussed Arafat's administration of stirring the protests.
